title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would bar the creation or operation of AI data‑center facilities on lands managed by the federal government. It aims to keep federal properties free from the large energy‑intensive data centers that are often built for AI workloads.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies that use automated decision systems to evaluate how their algorithms affect consumers and document any potential bias, discrimination, or privacy risks. It also establishes guidelines for transparency, auditing, and enforcement to help protect individuals from unfair or harmful algorithmic outcomes.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to shield the integrity of elections by curbing the use of deceptive artificial intelligence. It aims to regulate AI-generated content that could mislead voters and unfairly influence election outcomes.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act aims to shield families from the rising energy bills that result from the operation of AI data centers. It proposes regulatory measures or subsidies to reduce the cost impact on household budgets.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a legislative effort to regulate artificial intelligence technology within the Homestake jurisdiction. It sets out requirements for transparency, safety, and accountability, and creates oversight mechanisms to protect citizens and encourage responsible AI development.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: Congress endorses the Ratepayer Protection Pledge as a sound policy to keep electricity affordable for all Americans, from households to businesses and public facilities. The pledge also aims to ensure reliable energy supply while supporting the growth of AI and data center infrastructure nationwide.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 sets rules to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems. It requires companies to assess and report AI energy use, adopt energy‑efficient models, and follow guidelines to limit greenhouse gas emissions.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 aims to set clear rules for how data can be collected, stored, and used by AI systems, ensuring transparency and accountability in the industry. It also establishes safeguards to protect individuals’ privacy while encouraging responsible innovation in AI technologies.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that build and use automated decision systems to evaluate their algorithms for bias, discrimination, and harmful impacts. It also mandates that these firms disclose their findings and put safeguards in place to protect consumers and ensure fair, transparent use of AI technologies.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 sets out safety standards and regulations for AI‑powered toys sold to children. It requires manufacturers to meet specified safety criteria, submit their products for certification, and safeguard kids against risks such as data privacy violations, inappropriate content, and unsafe interactions.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is designed to protect the privacy of young individuals who use or are affected by AI technologies. It establishes strict guidelines on data collection, usage, and disclosure to safeguard children’s personal information and ensure their digital safety.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 sets up a national framework to oversee and coordinate the use of AI‑driven physical systems such as robots, drones, and autonomous vehicles. It requires companies, governments, and other stakeholders to share safety standards, data, and best practices so these technologies can work together safely and reliably.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act aims to broaden the use of AI technologies, making AI tools more widely available to businesses and the public. It also establishes guidelines for ethical, transparent, and secure deployment of AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act temporarily stops the construction and expansion of new data centers dedicated to AI technology. This pause is intended to allow lawmakers to assess environmental, economic, and regulatory impacts before AI data center projects resume.

title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026
action: Star Print ordered on the bill.
summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 is designed to boost AI research and deployment by offering government funding, tax incentives, and streamlined regulatory approvals. It also seeks to protect the public by establishing safety standards, ethical guidelines, and oversight mechanisms for emerging AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act is a law designed to make data easier to use by artificial intelligence systems. It establishes standards and guidelines for collecting, labeling, and sharing data so that AI developers can build and improve models more efficiently and responsibly.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for assessing the potential risks of AI systems before they are released, requiring developers to conduct and report thorough risk evaluations to regulators. It also demands transparency in how AI decisions are made and imposes penalties for companies that fail to meet these safety and disclosure standards, aiming to protect public safety and privacy.

title: CREATE AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The CREATE AI Act is a proposed law designed to regulate the development, use, and oversight of artificial intelligence technologies. It aims to ensure that AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with ethical and societal norms.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act establishes rules for using AI technologies in veterinary medicine, aiming to improve animal care while safeguarding ethical standards. It sets clear guidelines for safety, transparency, and accountability so that AI tools support veterinarians, protect patient data, and promote animal welfare.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2026 is a law designed to strengthen AI education across the United States. It establishes federal funding and support for schools, teachers, and research institutions to develop AI curricula, training programs, and opportunities for students and educators.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to give small businesses access to AI training, resources, and funding so they can learn how to develop and use artificial‑intelligence technologies. By providing education, tools, and financial support, the act seeks to help entrepreneurs integrate AI into their operations, boosting innovation and competitiveness for small‑business owners.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act is a legislative proposal designed to help small businesses adopt and develop artificial intelligence technologies. It provides grants, tax incentives, and streamlined regulatory processes to lower barriers and encourage innovation among small enterprises.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed set of rules designed to make the use of artificial intelligence safer and more transparent. It outlines guidelines for AI developers and operators, including accountability standards and protections for users.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law designed to make the use of artificial‑intelligence technologies more transparent and fair. It aims to set clear rules and standards for AI systems so they are accountable and protect people from possible negative impacts.

title: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act is a law designed to protect people from fraud that uses artificial intelligence. It sets rules and penalties for companies that create or use AI to deceive or scamp consumers.

title: States' Right to Regulate AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act affirms that individual states have the authority to create and enforce their own rules governing the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence. It aims to give states the power to address local concerns—such as privacy, safety, and fairness—without needing federal regulation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 is proposed legislation designed to protect individuals from discrimination and bias caused by AI systems. It establishes standards for transparency, accountability, and equal treatment in the design, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 aims to build a skilled workforce for AI and other vital technologies so the United States stays competitive. It proposes training programs, education incentives, and support for companies to develop the talent needed for these high‑impact fields.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act is a legislative proposal aimed at increasing public understanding of artificial intelligence. It seeks to establish programs, resources, and outreach efforts that inform citizens about AI’s benefits, risks, and implications for society.

title: TEST AI Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The TEST AI Act of 2025 aims to establish guidelines for the use and development of artificial intelligence in the United States. It seeks to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with national security and ethical standards.

title: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025 establishes rules to identify and limit AI tools developed by or linked to hostile foreign entities, aiming to protect national security. It creates a regulatory framework for risk assessment, monitoring, and enforcement to prevent foreign adversarial AI from compromising critical systems and sensitive data.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for how small businesses can adopt and use artificial intelligence technologies. It aims to promote responsible innovation while protecting consumers, employees, and national security.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires that any AI system capable of modifying its own code or behavior be continuously monitored to ensure it operates safely and transparently. It establishes reporting standards, oversight mechanisms, and compliance rules so that developers can demonstrate that the AI remains under human control and does not pose unforeseen risks.

title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act is a proposed law that would require developers and users of generative AI systems to evaluate how those tools could be misused for terrorist purposes. It would mandate regular risk assessments, reporting to federal authorities, and the implementation of safeguards to reduce the potential for AI‑assisted terrorist activity.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes regulations to reduce the environmental footprint of AI technologies, focusing on energy consumption, carbon emissions, and resource use. It sets standards, reporting requirements, and incentives for organizations to adopt energy‑efficient AI models and greener infrastructure.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is legislation that bars artificial intelligence from providing medical diagnoses or treatments, insisting that only licensed human doctors can deliver such services. The act aims to protect patients by ensuring human oversight, imposes penalties for violations, and sets clear standards for any AI tools used in medical contexts.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: This act encourages companies to export the entire AI technology stack—hardware, software, and training—to foreign markets. By doing so, it aims to boost economic growth and maintain a competitive edge in global AI innovation.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act encourages major AI developers to make their models, code, and datasets publicly available to promote transparency and innovation. It establishes guidelines and incentives for sharing AI resources, aiming to build a competitive yet responsible ecosystem that benefits the broader public.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 aims to make sure AI systems used for veterans are safe, fair, and respect privacy. It establishes guidelines and oversight to protect veterans’ rights and well‑being when they interact with AI technologies.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law that aims to make advanced artificial intelligence systems safer and more secure. It seeks to set standards, require risk assessments, and ensure developers implement strong security measures to protect against misuse and unintended harms.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 is a law designed to reduce unfairness in automated decision‑making tools. It requires companies to test, document, and fix bias in their algorithms, and sets federal standards for transparency and accountability.
